To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

guinea pig lung alveolar macrophages (LAMs) secrete a potent chemoattractive factor (CAF) for neutrophils (PMNs), macrophages (MØs), and lymphocytes (LNs) that is released in a time-dependent manner and that the CAF is not cytotoxic to the LAMs.
guinea pig alveolar macrophages sequestered from the lungs of healthy animals are able to synthesize and secrete chemotaxins for neutrophils (PMN), macrophages and lymphocytes.
lung macrophages are able to produce a wide spectrum of chemotactic mediators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the secretion of chemotaxin by lung macrophages, a cell type which is thought to be important in the initiation and regulation of inflammation in the lungs.
the study of the mechanisms of inflammation, particularly the role of the macrophage in inflammation and the role of the lymphocyte in inflammation.
the study of the mechanisms by which macrophages participate in the inflammatory response to inhaled particulate antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lung macrophages are capable of secreting chemotactic activity for all of the inflammatory cells that participate in pulmonary inflammatory reactions.
the lung macrophages, when cultured in vitro, secrete chemotactic substances which can attract and stimulate the movement of lymphocytes, neutrophils and macrophages.

the lung macrophages of guinea pigs, when stimulated by phagocytosis, produce and secrete a number of chemotactic factors for neutrophils as well as lymphocytes, and that these factors are not toxic to the cells producing them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that lung macrophages, like peritoneal macro phages and other cells, can secrete chemotaxis.
the lung macrophages are able to secrete chemotaxins that are capable of inducing migration of inflammatory cells to the site of injury or inflammation.
macrophages are a major source of inflammatory mediators in the lung, which can be activated by a wide range of stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
macrophages are not just the garbage collectors of our body.
the cells that are most responsible for the inflammatory response are also the most responsible for the resolution of inflammation.
the lung macrophage is an important cell in the inflammatory process.
